language.script_notes: Rioplatense Spanish (distinctive 'vos' usage and sh/zh pronunciation of 'll'/'y', not visible in text but reflected in signage phrasing). Street suffixes: Calle, Avenida, Pasaje, Camino, Boulevard, Ramble.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Distinctive chevron-marked bollards and kilometer-marker posts along highways.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Varies; chevron road-curve markers are a strong general Argentina tell.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel W-beam on major routes; often minimal or absent on rural roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: White outside/white inside is common, with white outside/yellow inside also seen.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in cities; minimal shoulder definition on rural roads.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Chevron curve-warning signs and kilometer markers are distinctive nationally. YPF (the state oil company), Puma, Esso/Axion and Refinor are common fuel-station brands. Correo Argentino is the postal service brand.

architecture.roof_style: Low-pitch tile or metal roofs on estancia-style ranch buildings in the Pampas; flat adobe roofs in the Andean northwest; European-influenced architecture in Buenos Aires.
architecture.roof_material: Varies sharply by region — see regional profiles.
architecture.wall_construction: Spanish colonial-influenced estancia (ranch) architecture with thick adobe walls and exposed wood beams in rural areas; ornate European (French/Italian/Spanish-influenced) architecture in Buenos Aires; flat-roofed adobe construction in the Andean northwest.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Varies by region — see regional profiles.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Ornate Parisian-style apartment buildings and boulevards in central Buenos Aires; rustic estancia ranch buildings in the Pampas; colourful colonial adobe villages in the Andean northwest; nothing comparable in the vast empty Patagonian steppe.

nature.vegetation: Extremely varied by latitude — flat fertile grassland (Pampas) around Buenos Aires, dry Patagonian steppe scrub in the south, and Andean puna desert with cacti/hardy shrubs in the northwest. See regional profiles.
nature.terrain: One of the most latitudinally diverse countries on Earth — vast flat plains in the center, the Andes running the full western border, Patagonian steppe and glaciers in the far south.
nature.climate_signature: Humid temperate around Buenos Aires/the Pampas; cold, dry and windswept in Patagonia; high-altitude arid in the Andean northwest.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with a blue top strip carrying the Argentine flag and 'ARGENTINA' text (Mercosur standard since 2016); older plates (pre-2016) were black background with white text.
vehicles.plate_format: AA 000 AA (Mercosur format); older format was ABC 123.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Ford (long local manufacturing history — Falcon, Ranchero), Volkswagen (Gol/Gacel/Senda) and Fiat all have a long domestic-assembly history and are disproportionately common.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Argentina uses a distinctive black Google car (shared with only Peru and Uruguay in South America) on Gen 3 coverage; Gen 4 coverage is limited to the area north of Comodoro Rivadavia, meaning most of Patagonia is still Gen 3.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense around Buenos Aires and the Pampas; progressively sparser moving into Patagonia and the remote northwest.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same Rioplatense Spanish region, similar Pampas-style grassland near the shared border, similar Mercosur plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Uruguay's plates and bollards trend almost entirely white without Argentina's darker plate center; Uruguay's roads commonly show triple-lined markings rarely seen in Argentina; the Google car's front is more consistently ghostly pale in Uruguay.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Andes mountain border, some overlapping Patagonian terrain in the far south
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chile is a narrow north-south strip dominated by the Pacific side of the Andes and often shows the white rear of the Google car; Argentina's terrain is broader and flatter to the east of the Andes, with its own black-car Gen 3 coverage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Spanish language, some shared flat subtropical terrain in northern Argentina
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Paraguay is bilingual with Guaraní appearing alongside Spanish on some signage, which doesn't occur in Argentina; plate and road-furniture details differ once compared directly.
